# Summary of Studienstiftung
The Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes, originally founded in Dresden in 1925 as part of the Deutsche Studentenschaft, was dissolved during National Socialism in 1934 and re-established in Cologne as a registered association in 1948. It is a prestigious German scholarship foundation that selects exceptionally talented students and doctoral candidates based on principles of excellence, initiative, and responsibility. Admission occurs through various channels including nominations by schools, university professors, examination boards, competition winners, assessment tests, alumni, and support for musicians and artists. Selection involves interviews and group discussions assessing academic merit as well as social commitment, with admission rates varying by nomination channel.
The Studienstiftung provides both financial and academic support. Financial aid includes a monthly allowance, health insurance subsidies, and need-based scholarships, which for PhD students amount to €1,550 monthly (rising in 2025). Academic support consists of summer schools, research groups, language courses, workshops, mentoring, and opportunities to organize conferences. In 2023, the foundation approved nearly 2,500 scholarships, encompassing undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels, representing about 0.48% of German students. It also partners with institutions such as King Abdullah University of Science and Technology for research internships and offers various internal and open scholarship programs. Notable alumni include numerous Nobel laureates and leading figures across sciences, social sciences, business, politics, arts, and journalism.
